name: CTAO telescope arrays

technology.value: Two ground-based arrays of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in three size classes (Large, Medium, Small).
technology.quote: four Large-Sized Telescopes... up to 23 Medium-Sized Telescopes... up to 37 Small-Sized Telescopes

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: The construction and operation of the CTAO is a global initiative
intervals.note: 2015 is a lower bound only (the year INSPIRE's CTA experiment record was created); no fetched source this session gives a construction-start date.

telescope_count.quote: four Large-Sized Telescopes... up to 23 Medium-Sized Telescopes... up to 37 Small-Sized Telescopes
telescope_count.note: Sum of the design maximums (4 LST + 23 MST + 37 SST = 64) stated across CTAO's technology page; not itself a single quoted total figure.

description.value: Four Large-Sized Telescopes planned in the northern array (La Palma) for the lowest energies, 20 GeV to 3 TeV.
description.quote: four Large-Sized Telescopes in the northern hemisphere for its low-energy range... 20 GeV to 3 TeV

description.value: Up to 23 Medium-Sized Telescopes distributed over both array sites, covering 80 GeV to 50 TeV.
description.quote: up to 23 Medium-Sized Telescopes distributed over both array sites... 80 GeV to 50 TeV

description.value: Up to 37 Small-Sized Telescopes planned in the southern array (Paranal) for the highest energies, above 2 TeV.
description.quote: up to 37 Small-Sized Telescopes in the southern hemisphere... above 2 TeV

summary.plain: Two big groups of gamma-ray telescopes, one in Spain and one in Chile, coming in three different sizes so together they can see the whole range of gamma-ray energies.
summary.technical: Imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov arrays at two sites (La Palma / Paranal), using Large-, Medium- and Small-Sized Telescope classes (design maximum 4 LST + 23 MST + 37 SST) to cover 20 GeV-300 TeV; under construction as of the sources fetched this session.

notes: document_ids deliberately not written (v0.2 A1 derived field).
Per-site current telescope counts (how many of each class are actually installed and operating today, as opposed to the design maximums) were not sourced this session.
